title: Demon's Catalyst
snippet:
Demon's Catalyst -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Demon's Catalyst is the second-heaviest catalyst in the game to the Manus Catalyst, which weighs one unit more. It has one of the lowest potential magic adjusts of any catalyst, being the lowest until 41 Intelligence where it surpasses the Oolacile Ivory Catalyst and Oolacile Catalyst. It trades these things for being a powerful melee weapon, dealing Fire and Thrust damage with its strong attack. The high strength and dexterity scaling will have a powerful effect on dark sorceries, as the physical damage dealt by those sorceries are boosted by those stats. Overall the Demon's Catalyst should be considered as a weapon that is effective with dark sorceries, but is not as effective with regular sorceries.

title: Archdeacon's Great Staff
snippet: It should not be confused with the Crystal Chime, which can cast Sorceries and Miracles based on leveling Intelligence and Faith equally, or the Izalith Staff, which is designed for Dark Sorceries. The Golden Ritual Spear is a hybrid weapon that can also function as a staff, and operates on the same principle as the Archdeacon's Great Staff. The Man-grub's Staff is another staff that scales off of a stat that is not Intelligence.

title: Archdeacon's Great Staff
snippet:
Archdeacon's Great Staff -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Although it is a staff, the Archdeacon's Great Staff scales purely off of Faith rather than Intelligence. As such, it is designed to be used by builds with high amounts of Faith and utility amounts of Intelligence. Although this requires a high investment in levels into multiple stats, the benefit is that it allows high Faith builds to cast Sorceries with power on par with their Miracles. This allows it to be utilized on very unconventional builds, as both Lightning Stake and Great Heavy Soul Arrow can be cast on the same character to devastating effect.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
The Assassin Set has only moderate physical defences but has good magic and fire defences, and high overall resistances against anything that isn't Bleed.

While the **Assassin** doesn't have any ranged attack, its Spook Sorcery is extremely useful for removing most non-fatal fall damage and for completely silencing footsteps for 20 seconds, allowing certain obstacles to be bypassed . Unfortunately, while the starting Sorcerer's Staff is a fairly good spell tool, if not exactly the best, it won't actually start to gain scaling from stats until Intelligence has reached at least 19, delaying a possible strengthening of the character's Sorceries.

Picking up the Soul Arrow Sorcery from the Shrine Handmaid gives a reusable ranged attack early on, while the weapon buffing Magic Weapon Sorcery can be gained in either Undead Settlement or Road of Sacrifices to add some of a Staff's spellbuff to weapon damage.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
Assassin (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Assassin** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Dexterity-based class with decent Attunement for Weapon Arts and spells and some Intelligence for Sorceries.

An unusually long Thrusting Sword, the Estoc is also quite strong and has a rare sweeping heavy attack for hitting several or agile foes easier, at the cost of not having an increased critical modifier for Ripostes and Backstabs. Additionally, its Weapon Art, Shield Splitter, helps with its bad damage to the stamina of blocking targets by partially bypassing the defences of the block instead.

Its Targeting Shield, while not very suitable for blocking, is one of the game's three parrying shields and as such its Parry starts slightly earlier yet ends as late as the regular parry.

The Assassin Set has only moderate physical defences but has good magic and fire defences, and high overall resistances against anything that isn't Bleed.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
Assassin (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : This class is fairly popular amongst speedrunners thanks to Spook making it possible to easier skip foes and falls.
While the Assassin doesn't have any direct equivalent class in the Dark Souls series, it does bear some resemblance to the Royalty class from FromSoftware's previous game Demon's Souls, another Dexterity/Intelligence-based class wielding a thrusting sword (in that case a Rapier) and a small shield while also providing access to a Sorcery-like spell (though in the Royalty's case it is the offensive Soul Arrow, not a self-buffing spell).

title: Attunement (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Attunement (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : Attunement determines the number of spell slots the player has available to equip spells, and also increases the player's Cast Speed (this effect is roughly double that of leveling Intelligence or Faith). In addition to these, raising Attunement also increases the number of casts per slot a spell has; however, this varies from spell to spell. Raising Attunement also increases the player's Curse Resist and Agility slightly, and as with every other stat, HP is increased by minute amounts each time.

**20/25/30** are the softcaps for attunement that you’d generally want to stop at for a caster build in terms of spell slots. The caps for attunement are **30/75** for spell slots, **94** for max number of spell casts, and around **50-55** for spell casting speed in conjunction with 50 Faith or Intelligence.

title: Attunement (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Attunement (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - notes 
 notes : Players that want to make the most out of Attunement without investing fully in it should note that most spells that have very little uses, will be almost maxed out at 49. Most spells that have a maximum of 3 uses will be at 2, those that have a maximum of 4 will be at 3, and the same math applies to all those that have 5 and 6 maximum uses. This is important to take into consideration should players want to make Faith or Pyromancy builds, as most spells of those categories are often of very low uses.

title: Attunement (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Attunement (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Attunement** is a stat in *Dark Souls III* that increases the player character's Focus Points, or FP as well as increasing the number of Attunement slots.

Focus Points are used to cast Sorceries, Pyromancies and Miracles, as well as performing skills.

Spells can be attuned at the bonfire, provided the player has available Attunement slots. A minimum investment of 10 Attunement is required for one Attunement slot.

As it is with every other stat in the game, it also has indirect bonuses such as increasing the player character's flat defenses.

Leveling Attunement provides the following benefits:

Diminishing returns for increasing the amount of FP begin at 35 Attunement, while every 10 Attunement past 30 (except at 80 Attunement) will grant an additional slot. Equipping any one of the Saint's Ring, Deep Ring and Darkmoon Ring will grant 1, 1 and 2 additional Attunement slots, respectively.

title: Attunement (Dark Souls III)
snippet: At 99 Attunement, the player will have 450 FP and 10 Attunement slots.

Softcaps for Attunement are **16/19/23** with 50 being the hardcap for spell slots. Leveling Attunement beyond 50 gives no benefits aside from a couple points in various defenses. For a caster build it is not advisable to level Attunement beyond 23.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bandit (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bandit** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 2*.

It has high Dexterity and well above average Faith, meaning it lends itself rather well towards builds focused either on both or only the former (though it will have strong competition from the Swordsman when it comes to pure Dexterity builds). It is rather unsuitable to spells, even the Miracle ones, due to its extremely low Attunement and Intelligence.

Bandits are actually unable to speak to Straid of Olaphis by default, the only class that can't do that, due to its extremely low Intelligence not meeting his minimum required amount of 3.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet: There is a curious disadvantage to its high Vitality, higher than any other starting class: when using the Third Dragon Ring, it cannot receive the full benefit of the Flynn's Ring and will get a light decrease of 4 Attack Rating compared to any other class.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Until an unlimited source of arrows is acquired, they are best either saved for trying to pull individual enemies from groups or ambushes, or for trying to kill one of the early Ogres (either the one outside the Firekeeper's Hut in Things Betwixt at the start of the tutorial that also holds the Stone Ring, or the Scholar of the First Sin-exclusive one on the way towards the Forest of Fallen Giants) for a large amount of extra Souls.

The class's Bandit Set is actually fairly good, as it has somewhat high physical defences and is, together with the Knight's partial Falconer Set, the only starting set with decent starting Poise.

Due to its very low Adaptability and Attunement it has a substandard roll (only 7 i-frames, compared to most other classes having 8 or 9 i-frames) and needs 3 points in Adaptability or 9 points in Attunement to improve this to 8 i-frames.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bandits are actually unable to speak to Straid of Olaphis by default, the only class that can't do that, due to its extremely low Intelligence not meeting his minimum required amount of 3.

The starting weapons are somewhat mixed, with the Short Bow following the higher starting value in Dexterity while the Hand Axe instead focuses on Strength. The Hand Axe is most likely better replaced with an actually Dexterity-focused weapon, though those are in limited supply until Blacksmith Lenigrast's shop is opened, mostly the Dagger in Things Betwixt and the Halberd in the Forest of Fallen Giants. Beyond extra weapons such as the Spear and the Rapier, Lenigrast also holds the game's first infinite supply of ammunition (merely more Wood Arrows, but still) and another Short Bow.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : is a character in *Dark Souls*. First met in Sen's Fortress, from which he relocates to Firelink Shrine, he is a merchant of advanced sorceries, including new ones upon following his questline into The Duke's Archives.

Voiced by Ian Thompson in his final role before his passing in 2022, Logan is also a mentioned character in *Dark Souls II* and a mentioned character in *Dark Souls III*, although *Dark Souls II* refers to him as an unnamed "master sorcerer" due to his name being forgotten in Drangleic.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Master Logan was a famous Sorcerer and a royal member of the Vinheim Dragon School before he turned Undead about one hundred years ago. His nickname stems from the gigantic hat he wore which completely hid his face; he used it to block the noise and stares from those around him in order to focus his thoughts. His weapon was once an ordinary catalyst employed by the Sorcerers of Vinheim, but it has since been strengthened due to lengthy use over time. His sage robe, called prototype, meaning it goes back the School foundation of the Dragon School, therefore the School was founded around the times Logan was alive.

Logan is credited with having developed the Soul Spear Sorcery, among others, which is referenced repeatedly in the legends and is said to be on par with Lord Gwyn's lightning.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Big Hat Logan seems to prefer sitting down in a meditative position, except for the first encounter when he's in a hanging jail cage.
If you get the Man-Serpent leaning against the wall next to the cage he is in, It will break, meaning you don't need to get the boulder trap to break it, with careful planning.
Logan shares many similarities with Sage Freke from *Demon's Souls*. Both are first found trapped in cages and rescued by the player. Both are preceded by apprentices looking for them, have an unhealthy fascination with magic, and are found sitting in the main hub area.
Rickert of Vinheim mentions to the player that Big Hat Logan is famous in Vinheim; however, he also mentions that Logan was from "a hundred years ago". Either Logan has remained sane for as long as he has been undead, or time warping in Lordran has brought Logan to a time where one does not belong.

title: Sorcery (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Sorcery (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - spell - general_information 
 general_information : Sorceries are cast by catalysts. Catalysts scale with the Intelligence stat, with the unique exception of Tin Darkmoon Catalyst, which scales with Faith.

Most sorceries can be purchased from various merchants found throughout the game. Some are found as lootable items.

There are more sorceries than either pyromancies or miracles. While pyromancies focus on offensive spells and miracles focus on defensive and healing, sorceries include a variety of utility and augmentation spells as well as a range of offensive spells.

All forms of offensive sorceries cause Magic Damage, which is typically effective against iron armor, tough scales, and other physically resilient materials.

title: Spell (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Spell (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : Spells are broken down into four classes: sorceries, miracles, pyromancies, and hexes.

Each spell type is cast with a catalyst: staves for sorcery, sacred chimes for miracles, pyromancy flames for pyromancy, and staves or sacred chimes for hexes. In addition, each spell type is associated with a magic type: Magic for sorcery, Lightning for miracles, Fire for pyromancy, and Dark for hexes.

Casting a spell sometimes necessitates meeting the minimum attribute requirements: Intelligence for sorceries, Faith for miracles, and a mixture of both Intelligence and Faith for hexes. Pyromancies are unique in that they have no attribute requirements to cast.

title: Sorcerer
snippet:
Sorcerer -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Sorcerer** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls*.

This class' primary form of attack is through casting sorceries, and start the game with the Soul Arrow sorcery. However, their high Attunement and Intelligence means they can make the use of either sorceries and/or pyromancies.

Sorcerers' expertise in sorceries are at the expense of having poor physical damage output. Their dexterity, unlike their strength, is decent, however.

For new players playing blind, Sorcerers can be tricky, since the merchants for the other spells must be found before new spells can be obtained.

title: Elemental Damage
snippet:
Elemental Damage -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : There are three types of Elemental Damage: Magic, Fire and Lightning. Each have a corresponding defense stat that they are measured against. Because of this, certain elemental damage may be ineffective against certain enemies, while other forms of damage will be very effective.

Elemental Damage can be inflicted by casting numerous sorceries, miracles and pyromancies. Offensive spells almost always exclusively deal some form of elemental damage.

Weapons that inflict elemental damage almost always inflict a form of physical damage as well. The exceptions are the Moonlight Greatsword, Moonlight Butterfly Horn, Crystal Ring Shield and Moonlight Arrows, which all deal only Magic Damage, and the Pyromancy Flame, which deals only Fire Damage when used as a striking weapon.

title: Pyromancy (Dark Souls)
snippet: Unlike Sorcery and Miracles, Pyromancies are unique in that they do not require a specific stat level, or scale with any stat. Rather, players may upgrade their Pyromancy Flame 15 times at any pyromancy teacher, then ascend once and upgrade their Ascended Pyromancy flame another 5 times to increase their damage output. This means that players can use a high level Pyromancy Flame to deal high damage at low soul levels – making it useful for PvP. (Note, the Ascended Pyromancy Flame does not scale with intelligence, despite the item indicating such)

title: Spell Buff
snippet:
Spell Buff -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - overview 
 overview : Upon acquiring a catalyst, be it a Sacred Chime, a Talisman, a Staff, a Pyromancy Flame, or even weapons capable of casting spells (see "Unique Catalysts" for a list of such items), the stat that determines how effective it is at casting is its **Spell Buff**. This number is determined by the amount of Intelligence and Faith of the player (and in the case of one Staff, Luck).

A Staff with 130 Spell Buff will generally outperform one that has 120, if they were to cast the same Sorcery. The same holds true in any catalyst using their appropriate spell, with exception of Dark Spells.

In the *Souls* series, snakes and serpents are generally conceived as a type of lesser dragons, perhaps explaining the Man Serpents appearance in Archdragon Peak, their ability to spew fireballs, and why they worship the ancient dragons as their ancestors.

title: Fire Keeper
snippet:
In *Dark Souls II*, the three Fire Keepers in Things Betwixt and the Emerald Herald, believed by some to be Fire Keeper, can be killed without the nearby bonfire being affected. The way the Herald can level up the Bearer of the Curse is reminescent of how the Fire Keepers in *Dark Souls III* can the Ashen One. One of the Keepers, Strowen, offers the player to re-allocate their attributes in exchange for a Soul Vessel.

In *Dark Souls III*, the unnamed Fire Keeper can level up the Ashen One like the Hemerald did in the previous game. She is also immortal; killing her, in addition to not causing the Shrine bonfire to be affected, will only cause her to respawn upon reloading the area, claiming that she cannot die. Instead of a Keeper, it is Rosaria, Mother of Rebirth, the leader of the Rosaria's Fingers covenant, who allows the player to re-allocate their attributes.

title: Sorcery (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Sorcery (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - spell - lore 
 lore : Sorcery is said to have originated with Seath the Scaleless, the "grandfather of sorcery". The ancient land of Oolacile has its own sorceries, which are an "approximation" when compared to modern Sorcery and are characterized by augmenting the weapon or body, rather than causing offensive damage. Manus, Father of the Abyss is the source of at least one Abyss sorcery.

The other Abyss sorceries are said to be discovered by an Oolacile sorcerer on the brink of madness, they differ from normal offensive sorceries, which are derived from souls, in that they draw power from humanity and cause both Magic and Physical Damage due to their "weighty" nature.

Big Hat Logan of the Dragon School in Vinheim played a role in the development of numerous sorceries. During his infatuation with Seath in the Regal Archives, Logan developed new sorceries and boosted existing ones.

As *Berserk* happened to be among the favorite mangas of Hidetaka Miyazaki (the director of the *Dark Souls* franchise) and that he even approved how Catarina Set being based on Bazuso's armor, it's no surprise there are allusions to the aforementioned manga series in the game series proper. In Knight Artorias' case, he may very well influenced by Guts the Black Swordsman;

title: Pyromancy Flames
snippet:
Pyromancy Flames -  Dark Souls II - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Flames** are casting tools for Pyromancies in *Dark Souls II*, and are the only casting tools in the game which are able to cast them. They are unique amongst casting tools for the cheapness of upgrading them, in that only the cost of Souls needed to upgrade them increases; the player will only ever need one Fire Seed per upgrade. However, this is counterbalanced by the fact that Fire Seeds are found sporadically throughout the game.

title: Dark Souls II
snippet:
Dark Souls II -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - gameplay 
 gameplay : Similar to the previous title, players customize the gender and physical features of their character, in addition to choosing a starting class, which determines the stats and equipment that the player begins with, and a starting gift. From a third-person perspective, players explore a continuous, open world that is roughly the same size as the original game, but with more freedom in how the player can progress. Akin to the notorious difficulty of its predecessor, players are confronted by a persistently hostile environment with unrelenting enemies and bosses – death is a central theme. As enemies are defeated, souls are accumulated, acting as both a form of currency and means to increase attributes. Unlike the first game, however, the player can have a voice chat with other players in their world.

title: Pyromancy (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Pyromancy (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - spell - lore 
 lore : Before the creation of Pyromancy, flame sorceries were used by the Witch of Izalith, her Daughters of Chaos, and they later taught it to the Demon Firesages. The Witch and her daughters used flame sorcery to challenge the ancient dragons, casting it from catalysts just as soul sorceries were. In the wake of her attempt to recreate the First Flame, the Witch of Izalith and some of her daughters were engulfed in the newly formed Bed of Chaos. The witches mastered the power of the Flame of Chaos and gave birth to the Pyromancy and all knowledge of flame sorcery has since vanished.

Quelana of Izalith, a Daughter of Chaos, managed to flee the catastrophe created by her mother. Quelana, who is credited as one of the "mothers of pyromancy", after escaping from Izalith, teaches her art to a select few students and now resides in Blighttown.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Giant (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - enemy - variants 
 variants : Giants specialize in several different types of combat and can be differentiated by their appearance. Giants use their brute strength to great effect. Many of the soldiers who invaded Drangleic used large clubs, or even just their fists in battle. Some giants utilized a form of pyromancy, while others were known to have the ability to produce toxic projectiles from their bodies.

title: Saint's Talisman
snippet:
Saint's Talisman -  Dark Souls III - weapon - description 
 description : Medium for casting miracles of the Gods.
Ivory talismans are given only to women clerics, and faith greatly affects their effectiveness.

There is a certain frailty to this talisman, which undermines the steadfastness granted by its Skill.

Skill: Unfaltering Prayer
Temporarily increases poise while casting miracles, preventing enemy attacks from interrupting prayer. Works while equipped in either hand.

title: Dexterous Conversion
snippet:
Dexterous Conversion -  Dark Souls II - spell - description 
 description : Sorcery used in swordplay. Transfers intelligence to dexterity.

Though sorcerers do battle using their intelligence, there are times when physical prowess is the only way to come out on top. This sorcery was developed to aid in such situations.

title: Stats (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Stats (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - attributes 
 attributes : Attributes are the base stats of a character. They govern several derived stats and determine which weapons and spells the character can use.

A character's initial attributes depend on the starting class selected by the player during character creation. They can be increased by leveling up the character at the Fire Keeper, or by equipping certain items.

Attribute points gained by leveling up can be redistributed by offering a Pale Tongue to Rosaria in the Cathedral of the Deep.
